name: HTML Fundamentals
description: 200 multiple-choice and text-answer questions covering core HTML: document structure, semantic elements, text formatting, lists, links, images and media, forms and validation, tables, global attributes, accessibility/ARIA, metadata, embedding, HTML5 interactive elements, character entities, deprecated markup, and HTML's history and versioning.
author: James Zedd

questions.prompt: Which line must appear as the very first line of an HTML5 document?
questions.explanation: The doctype declaration (an HTML5 doctype is just `<!DOCTYPE html>`) must be the first thing in the document so browsers render in standards mode instead of quirks mode.

questions.prompt: Which two elements are the direct children of the html element in a standard document, in order?
questions.explanation: A conforming HTML document's root html element contains exactly one head element followed by one body element.

questions.prompt: Which element contains metadata about a document, such as its title and linked stylesheets, and is not displayed as page content? (one word)
questions.explanation: The head element holds machine-readable metadata: title, meta tags, links to stylesheets and scripts, none of which render as visible page content by default.

questions.prompt: Which element holds the visible content of an HTML page? (one word)
questions.explanation: Everything a browser renders on the page, text, images, forms, and so on, lives inside the body element.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on the html element tells assistive technology and browsers what language the page's text is written in? (one word, the attribute name only)
questions.explanation: The lang global attribute (e.g. lang="en") declares the primary language of the content, which screen readers use to choose pronunciation rules.

questions.prompt: Which attribute controls the base text direction of a document, such as right-to-left for Arabic or Hebrew?
questions.explanation: The dir global attribute accepts ltr, rtl, or auto and sets the base directionality of the element's text.

questions.prompt: Where should meta charset be placed for maximum reliability?
choices: As early as possible inside head
At the very end of body
It can only go in an external file
questions.explanation: Browsers only scan a limited number of bytes at the start of a document looking for the character encoding, so meta charset should be one of the first elements inside head.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the browser rendering mode triggered by a missing or malformed doctype? (two words)
questions.explanation: Without a valid doctype, browsers fall back to quirks mode, which emulates old, inconsistent rendering behavior instead of following the modern CSS/HTML specifications.

questions.prompt: What is the exact doctype declaration used to trigger standards mode in HTML5? (answer in lowercase with no trailing punctuation)
questions.explanation: HTML5 simplified the doctype down to a single, case-insensitive token: <!DOCTYPE html>.

questions.prompt: Why is meta charset usually written as UTF-8 rather than an older encoding like ISO-8859-1?
choices: UTF-8 can represent virtually every character from every writing system, avoiding mojibake
Browsers ignore the charset attribute entirely
questions.explanation: UTF-8 is a superset encoding capable of representing the full Unicode character set, so it is the recommended default and avoids garbled text (mojibake) for international content.

questions.prompt: Which of these is valid, minimal, well-formed HTML5 document structure?
choices: A document with only a body, no head
A document with doctype, html, head with title, and body
A document with two head elements
A document with body nested inside head
questions.explanation: A minimal conforming document needs a doctype, a single html root, one head (which should contain at least a title), and one body.

questions.prompt: Which element inside head controls the text shown in the browser tab and bookmarks? (one word)
questions.explanation: The title element's text is what browsers display in the tab, window title bar, history, and bookmarks; it is not rendered inside the page body.

questions.prompt: Which element represents the dominant, unique content of a document, and should appear only once per page? (one word)
questions.explanation: The main element wraps the content unique to the current page, excluding repeated site furniture like navigation and footers; a document should have at most one visible main.

questions.prompt: Which element is best suited for a page's top banner containing a logo and site title?
questions.explanation: The header element represents introductory content or a group of navigational aids, commonly used for a page or section's heading area.

questions.prompt: Which element is intended for a set of navigation links, such as a primary menu? (one word)
questions.explanation: The nav element marks up a section of major navigational links, helping assistive technology identify and let users skip to navigation.

questions.prompt: Which element represents content that is tangentially related to the surrounding content, like a sidebar or pull quote?
questions.explanation: aside represents content indirectly related to the main content, such as sidebars, callout boxes, or advertising.

questions.prompt: Which element is used for self-contained, independently distributable content, such as a blog post or news story? (one word)
questions.explanation: article represents a complete, self-contained composition that would make sense on its own, e.g. in a feed or when syndicated.

questions.prompt: Which element groups a thematic set of content, typically with its own heading, without implying it is independently distributable?
questions.explanation: section groups related content under a common theme, usually introduced by a heading, but unlike article it isn't meant to stand alone out of context.

questions.prompt: When should a plain div be preferred over section or article?
choices: When the grouping exists only for styling or scripting hooks, with no semantic meaning
Whenever the content has a heading
Whenever the content appears more than once on the page
Never, div is obsolete in HTML5
questions.explanation: div is a generic container with no semantic meaning; it should be used for styling/scripting grouping when none of the more specific sectioning elements fit.

questions.prompt: Which element typically holds copyright notices, related links, and author info at the bottom of a page or section?
questions.explanation: footer represents footer content for its nearest sectioning ancestor, commonly copyright, contact, and related-document links.

questions.prompt: Which element wraps a self-contained piece of content like an image, diagram, or code listing, optionally paired with a caption? (one word)
questions.explanation: figure groups media content with its figcaption, and the whole unit can be moved away from the main flow without affecting the document's meaning.

questions.prompt: Which element provides the caption for the content inside a figure element?
questions.explanation: figcaption is the dedicated caption element for figure, and can appear as the first or last child of its figure.

questions.prompt: Which element is intended for contact information for its nearest article or body ancestor? (one word)
questions.explanation: address represents contact information (physical address, email, phone, etc.) for the author of the nearest enclosing article or the whole document.

questions.prompt: Which element represents a specific period in time and can carry a machine-readable datetime attribute? (one word)
questions.explanation: time represents a specific date/time, and its datetime attribute lets you provide a machine-readable value alongside human-readable text.

questions.prompt: Can a page legitimately contain more than one nav element?
choices: No, nav can only be used once per page
Yes, e.g. one for primary navigation and another for a table of contents or breadcrumb trail
Only if each nav is hidden with the hidden attribute
questions.explanation: A document can have multiple nav elements, for example primary navigation, secondary navigation, and breadcrumbs, as long as each represents a major block of navigation links.

questions.prompt: A header element placed inside an article, rather than as a direct child of body, represents what?
choices: Introductory content scoped to that article, such as its title and byline
Nothing, header is invalid inside article
questions.explanation: header and footer are scoped to their nearest sectioning content or sectioning root ancestor, so a header inside an article describes that article's own introductory content, not the whole page.

questions.prompt: Which heading levels should generally be avoided skipping, for both accessibility and semantics?
choices: It's fine to skip from h1 straight to h4 for visual effect
Heading levels should form a logical outline without skipping levels
Only h1 matters, others are optional decoration
Heading order does not matter to assistive technology
questions.explanation: Screen reader users often navigate by heading level; skipping levels (e.g. h1 to h3) breaks the logical outline of the page even if it looks fine visually.

questions.prompt: Which element is the generic inline counterpart to div, carrying no semantic meaning on its own? (one word)
questions.explanation: span is a generic inline container used for styling or scripting hooks when no semantic inline element applies, mirroring div's role at the block level.

questions.prompt: Which element represents an extended quotation set off from the surrounding text as its own block? (one word)
questions.explanation: blockquote marks up a section quoted from another source, typically rendered as an indented block; a cite attribute can point to the source URL.

questions.prompt: Which element is used for a short, inline quotation rather than a block-level one?
questions.explanation: q wraps a short inline quotation; browsers typically add quotation marks around it automatically via CSS.

questions.prompt: Which element marks up the title of a work, like a book or movie, being referenced? (one word)
questions.explanation: cite represents the title of a creative work being referenced, and is commonly rendered in italics by default.

questions.prompt: Which element represents an abbreviation or acronym, and can carry a title attribute with the full expansion?
questions.explanation: abbr marks up an abbreviation; its optional title attribute can hold the expanded form, which browsers often show as a tooltip.

questions.prompt: Which element highlights text as relevant or of special interest, commonly rendered with a yellow background? (one word)
questions.explanation: mark represents text highlighted for reference purposes, such as search-term matches, and is distinct from strong (importance) or em (stress emphasis).

questions.prompt: What is the key semantic difference between strong and b?
choices: strong indicates strong importance; b is a stylistic bold with no semantic weight
b is deprecated and invalid in HTML5
strong changes text color; b changes font size
They are identical in every way
questions.explanation: strong conveys strong importance, seriousness, or urgency to assistive technology, while b simply offers stylistic bold text without implying extra importance.

questions.prompt: What is the key semantic difference between em and i?
choices: em is deprecated in favor of i
em indicates stress emphasis that changes meaning when read aloud; i marks text as being in an alternate voice or mood, like a technical term
i can only appear inside p elements
questions.explanation: em conveys stress emphasis (changing the sentence's meaning if read aloud), whereas i is used for text in an alternate voice, such as foreign words or taxonomic names, without implying emphasis.

questions.prompt: Which pair of elements together mark up text that was removed from, and text that was inserted into, a document (e.g. in a tracked revision)?
questions.explanation: del represents deleted content and ins represents inserted content, commonly used to show document edits.

questions.prompt: Which element renders text in a fixed-width font and preserves whitespace and line breaks exactly as written? (one word)
questions.explanation: pre preserves whitespace and line breaks from the source, rendering in a monospace font by default, commonly used for code listings or ASCII art.

questions.prompt: Which inline element marks up a short fragment of computer code within a sentence?
questions.explanation: code marks up a short inline span of computer code, rendered in a monospace font, without the whitespace-preservation of pre.

questions.prompt: Which two-letter HTML element renders text as subscript, such as the 2 in a chemical formula like H2O? (one word)
questions.explanation: sub renders its content as subscript text, positioned slightly below the baseline.

questions.prompt: Which two-letter HTML element renders text as superscript, such as an exponent? (one word)
questions.explanation: sup renders its content as superscript text, positioned slightly above the baseline.

questions.prompt: Which element creates an unordered (bulleted) list? (one word)
questions.explanation: ul creates an unordered list, whose items are typically rendered with bullet markers rather than numbers.

questions.prompt: Which element creates an ordered (numbered) list?
questions.explanation: ol creates an ordered list, rendering its items with sequential markers such as numbers or letters.

questions.prompt: Which element represents an individual item inside ul or ol? (one word)
questions.explanation: li marks up a single list item and is valid as a child of ul, ol, or menu.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on ol changes the number that the list begins counting from?
questions.explanation: The start attribute on ol sets the starting ordinal value for the list, overriding the default of 1.

questions.prompt: Which boolean attribute on ol displays the list numbers in descending order? (one word, the attribute name only)
questions.explanation: The reversed boolean attribute on ol numbers the list items in descending order instead of the default ascending order.

questions.prompt: Which pair of elements together builds a description (definition) list of terms and their descriptions?
choices: dt and dd, inside a dl
questions.explanation: dl is the description list container, whose children are dt (the term) and dd (the term's description), which can repeat in groups.

questions.prompt: Inside a dl element, which element wraps the term or name being defined? (one word)
questions.explanation: dt wraps the term (name) in a name/value group within a description list.

questions.prompt: Are lists allowed to nest, e.g. a ul inside an li of another ul?
choices: No, nested lists are invalid HTML
Yes, a full list is a valid child of a list item, producing a nested sublist
Only ol can nest inside ul, never the reverse
Only up to two levels of nesting are valid
questions.explanation: A ul or ol can be placed inside an li to create a nested sublist; there is no limit on nesting depth imposed by the spec.

questions.prompt: Which attribute of the anchor element specifies the link's destination?
questions.explanation: href (hypertext reference) holds the URL that the anchor element points to.

questions.prompt: Which value of the target attribute opens the link in a new browsing context, typically a new tab? (include the leading underscore)
questions.explanation: target="_blank" instructs the browser to open the link in a new tab or window, rather than the current one.

questions.prompt: When using target="_blank", which rel value should be added to prevent the new page from gaining a handle back to the opening window via window.opener?
choices: noreferrer only, noopener has no effect
questions.explanation: rel="noopener" prevents the newly opened page from accessing window.opener, closing off a class of tab-napping attacks; modern browsers apply this behavior by default for target=_blank but it's still recommended to set explicitly for older engines.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on an anchor element makes the browser download the linked resource instead of navigating to it? (one word)
questions.explanation: The download attribute on a tells the browser to save the linked URL rather than navigate to it, and can optionally specify a suggested filename.

questions.prompt: Which href URL scheme opens the user's email client with a prefilled recipient? (include the trailing colon, e.g. scheme:)
questions.explanation: A mailto: URL scheme, e.g. href="mailto:someone@example.com", opens the user's default mail client addressed to that recipient.

questions.prompt: Which href scheme creates a clickable link that dials a phone number on supporting devices?
questions.explanation: The tel: URL scheme, e.g. href="tel:+15551234567", lets supporting devices initiate a phone call when the link is activated.

questions.prompt: An href value of just "#section2" links to what?
choices: An element elsewhere on the same page whose id is section2
questions.explanation: A fragment-only href scrolls to, and links to, an element on the same page whose id matches the fragment.

questions.prompt: Which rel value tells search engines and crawlers not to pass ranking credit to the linked page, often used for sponsored or user-generated links? (one word)
questions.explanation: rel="nofollow" is a hint to search engines that the destination shouldn't be endorsed or have link authority passed to it, commonly used on ads and untrusted user content.

questions.prompt: Besides http(s):, mailto:, and tel:, which of these is also a valid href scheme supported natively by browsers?
choices: Both ftp: and sms: are valid schemes browsers can handle
Neither, only http(s) is valid in href
questions.explanation: Browsers support several URL schemes in href beyond http(s), including ftp: for file transfer links and sms: for prefilling a text message, though actual handling depends on the OS and installed apps.

questions.prompt: If an anchor element's target attribute is omitted entirely, what value does it effectively behave as, meaning the link opens in the current browsing context? (include the leading underscore)
questions.explanation: The implicit default for target is _self, so links open in the same browsing context they were clicked from unless target says otherwise.

questions.prompt: Which required attribute of the img element provides a fallback text description of the image's content? (one word)
questions.explanation: alt is a required accessibility attribute on img that provides a textual description standing in for the image.

questions.prompt: For a purely decorative image that adds no information, what should its alt attribute be set to?
questions.explanation: An empty alt="" tells assistive technology to skip the image entirely, which is correct for purely decorative images that convey no content.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the srcset attribute on img?
choices: To provide a fallback image if the src fails
To offer multiple image resources at different resolutions or widths, letting the browser pick the best one
To set a CSS background image
To lazily load the image only after page load
questions.explanation: srcset lists a set of candidate image URLs (often with width or pixel-density descriptors), letting the browser choose the most appropriate one for the current viewport and screen density.

questions.prompt: Which value of the img loading attribute defers loading an offscreen image until the user scrolls near it? (one word, the attribute value only)
questions.explanation: loading="lazy" on img (and iframe) tells the browser to defer fetching the resource until it's close to entering the viewport, improving initial page load performance.

questions.prompt: Which element lets you specify multiple image sources so the browser can pick the best format or size, falling back to an inner img? (one word)
questions.explanation: picture contains one or more source elements offering different formats/sizes plus a required fallback img, letting browsers choose the most suitable resource.

questions.prompt: Inside a picture element, which attribute on source specifies a media condition, like a minimum viewport width, for choosing that source?
questions.explanation: The media attribute on source takes a media-query-like condition; the browser uses the first matching source, falling back to the picture's img if none match.

questions.prompt: Which element embeds a video player, with built-in playback controls when the controls attribute is set? (one word)
questions.explanation: video embeds a video resource and, when given the controls attribute, exposes a native play/pause/volume UI.

questions.prompt: Which element embeds an audio player? (one word)
questions.explanation: audio embeds sound content, similarly to how video embeds visual media, and also supports the controls attribute.

questions.prompt: Which element, nested inside video or audio, provides multiple source files (e.g. different formats) with fallback?
questions.explanation: source lets you list multiple candidate media files for video/audio; the browser plays the first one whose type it can handle.

questions.prompt: Which element adds captions or subtitles to a video element? (one word)
questions.explanation: track, nested inside video, supplies timed text such as subtitles or captions, typically as a WebVTT file referenced by its src attribute.

questions.prompt: Which boolean video/audio attribute automatically restarts playback from the beginning once it ends?
questions.explanation: The loop boolean attribute makes video or audio playback restart automatically when it reaches the end.

questions.prompt: Why do browsers block autoplay of audio (and video with sound) by default on most sites?
choices: To prevent unwanted, disruptive sound from playing without direct user interaction
Because the autoplay attribute was removed from the HTML spec
Only because of low bandwidth concerns
questions.explanation: Browsers restrict autoplaying media with sound as a user-experience and abuse-prevention measure, generally requiring muted playback or prior user interaction with the site.

questions.prompt: Which element provides an immediate-mode drawing surface for 2D or WebGL graphics controlled via JavaScript? (one word)
questions.explanation: canvas exposes a bitmap drawing surface that JavaScript can paint onto using the Canvas 2D or WebGL APIs.

questions.prompt: How does svg differ fundamentally from canvas as a graphics technology in HTML?
choices: They are identical, just different tag names
svg describes graphics declaratively as a DOM of shape elements, while canvas is an imperative bitmap you paint on with script
canvas is for vector graphics; svg is for raster images
svg cannot be styled with CSS
questions.explanation: SVG builds a retained, inspectable DOM tree of vector shape elements that CSS and JS can target individually, whereas canvas is a single bitmap surface painted imperatively via script with no per-shape DOM.

questions.prompt: Which attribute pairs with srcset to tell the browser how wide the image will actually be displayed, helping it choose the right candidate?
questions.explanation: sizes describes the image's rendered display size (often via media-query-like conditions), which the browser combines with srcset's width descriptors to pick the best resource.

questions.prompt: Which value of the img loading attribute forces the browser to fetch it immediately at normal priority, the opposite of lazy? (one word, the attribute value only)
questions.explanation: loading="eager" is the default: it tells the browser to fetch the image right away regardless of whether it's currently in the viewport.

questions.prompt: Which element wraps a set of form controls that get submitted together? (one word)
questions.explanation: form is the container element that groups controls into a single submittable unit, with attributes like action and method controlling submission.

questions.prompt: Which form attribute specifies the URL that form data is submitted to?
questions.explanation: action holds the URL the form's data is sent to when submitted.

questions.prompt: Which form attribute chooses the HTTP method (e.g. GET or POST) used to submit the form?
questions.explanation: method sets the HTTP verb used for submission; GET appends data to the URL while POST sends it in the request body.

questions.prompt: Which element associates a text caption with a specific form control, improving both usability and accessibility? (one word)
questions.explanation: label ties descriptive text to a control, either by wrapping it or via its for attribute matching the control's id; clicking the label also focuses/activates the control.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on label must match a form control's id to associate them when the label doesn't wrap the control?
questions.explanation: label's for attribute references the id of the control it describes, creating a programmatic association even when they aren't nested.

questions.prompt: Which element groups related form controls together and can render a visible border around them? (one word)
questions.explanation: fieldset groups a set of related controls, often rendered with a default border, and can be disabled as a whole to disable every control inside it.

questions.prompt: Which element provides a caption for the group of controls inside a fieldset? (one word)
questions.explanation: legend is the dedicated caption element for fieldset, and must be its first child.

questions.prompt: Which attribute gives a form control the name used as the key when its value is submitted?
questions.explanation: name provides the key under which a control's value is sent in the submitted form data; id is for DOM/label references and is a separate concern.

questions.prompt: What does the button element's type="submit" do inside a form, which is also the default type if type is omitted?
choices: Resets all fields to their default values
Does nothing until JavaScript is attached
questions.explanation: A button (or input) with type="submit", which is the implicit default, triggers the form's submission when activated.

questions.prompt: What does a button with type="reset" do?
choices: Clears the browser's autofill data permanently
Resets all of the form's controls back to their initial default values
Deletes the form from the DOM
questions.explanation: type="reset" restores every control in the form to the value it had when the page loaded, discarding any user edits.

questions.prompt: Why is button type="button" needed for controls that shouldn't submit the form, such as a 'toggle password visibility' control?
choices: Because button's default type is submit, so an explicit type="button" prevents an accidental form submission
Because button elements always submit forms no matter what
type="button" is required for any button to render
It has no effect either way
questions.explanation: Since a button inside a form defaults to type="submit", any button meant only to run script (not submit) should be explicitly given type="button" to avoid triggering submission.

questions.prompt: Which multi-line text input element lets users enter free-form text spanning several lines? (one word)
questions.explanation: textarea provides a resizable, multi-line plain-text input area, unlike the single-line input type="text".

questions.prompt: Which attribute lets a browser suggest previously entered values for a field, based on the field's name and type?
questions.explanation: autocomplete hints to the browser whether and how it should offer to fill in a field from the user's stored data.

questions.prompt: Which form attribute disables the browser's built-in HTML validation entirely when the form is submitted? (one word, the attribute name only)
questions.explanation: The novalidate boolean attribute on form skips the browser's automatic constraint validation on submission (formnovalidate does the same, but as a per-submit-button override instead).

questions.prompt: Which input type renders a single-line box appropriate for a password, masking the characters typed? (one word, the type value only)
questions.explanation: type="password" masks entered characters and also signals to browsers/password managers that this is a credential field.

questions.prompt: Which input type is optimized for email addresses, offering basic built-in format validation? (one word, the type value only)
questions.explanation: type="email" tells the browser to validate the value looks like an email address and, on mobile, often shows an @-friendly keyboard.

questions.prompt: Which input type restricts entry to numeric values and often shows increment/decrement spinner controls? (one word, the type value only)
questions.explanation: type="number" constrains the field to numeric input and typically renders spinner arrows for incrementing/decrementing the value.

questions.prompt: Which input type renders as a draggable slider rather than a text box, for picking a value within a range?
questions.explanation: type="range" produces a slider control, commonly paired with min, max, and step attributes.

questions.prompt: Which input type renders a single checkbox that toggles between checked and unchecked? (one word, the type value only)
questions.explanation: type="checkbox" produces an independent on/off toggle; multiple checkboxes sharing a name each submit independently when checked.

questions.prompt: Which input type lets a user pick exactly one option from a mutually exclusive group sharing the same name? (one word, the type value only)
questions.explanation: type="radio" inputs that share the same name form a mutually exclusive group, where selecting one deselects the others.

questions.prompt: Which input type opens the operating system's native date picker and submits a value like 2026-09-18?
questions.explanation: type="date" presents a date picker (implementation varies by browser) and normalizes the value to the YYYY-MM-DD format.

questions.prompt: Which input type is dedicated to picking a time of day, independent of any date?
questions.explanation: type="time" lets the user pick just an hour and minute, without an associated date.

questions.prompt: Which input type combines both a date and a time, without any timezone information, into a single control?
questions.explanation: type="datetime-local" collects a local date and time with no timezone offset; the older type="datetime" (with timezone) was removed from the spec.

questions.prompt: Which input type opens a native color-picker swatch and returns a value formatted as a hex color?
questions.explanation: type="color" provides a color-picker UI whose value is normalized to a lowercase 7-character hex string like #ff0000.

questions.prompt: Which input type presents a file-selection dialog, letting the user upload one or more files? (one word, the type value only)
questions.explanation: type="file" opens the OS file picker; combined with the multiple attribute it can accept more than one file, and accept restricts allowed file types.

questions.prompt: Which input type stores a value that is submitted with the form but never rendered or editable by the user? (one word, the type value only)
questions.explanation: type="hidden" carries a value in the form's submitted data without displaying any visible control for it.

questions.prompt: Which input type is intended for telephone numbers, showing a phone-style keypad on mobile but performing no built-in format validation?
questions.explanation: type="tel" hints at a phone-number keyboard on mobile devices, but unlike email or url it does not enforce any particular format by default, since phone number formats vary so widely.

questions.prompt: Which input type is meant for entering a web address and validates that the value is a syntactically valid URL? (one word, the type value only)
questions.explanation: type="url" checks that the entered value parses as a valid absolute URL before the form is considered valid.

questions.prompt: Which input type is styled like a text field but adds a clear ('x') button and is intended for search boxes?
questions.explanation: type="search" behaves much like plain text but is styled and semantically marked as a search field, and some browsers add a built-in clear control.

questions.prompt: Which element renders a dropdown list of predefined choices? (one word)
questions.explanation: select renders a dropdown (or list box, with the multiple attribute) built from nested option elements.

questions.prompt: Inside a select element, which element groups related option elements under a shared, non-selectable label?
questions.explanation: optgroup wraps a set of option elements and gives them a shared label, visually grouping related choices in the dropdown.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on a checkbox or radio input makes the browser render it in the checked state initially?
questions.explanation: The checked boolean attribute pre-selects a checkbox or radio input when the page loads.

questions.prompt: Which boolean attribute prevents a form from being submitted until a field has a value? (one word)
questions.explanation: The required attribute makes a field a constraint that must be satisfied before the browser allows the form to submit.

questions.prompt: Which attribute restricts a text-like input's value to match a given regular expression? (one word)
questions.explanation: pattern supplies a JavaScript-flavored regular expression the field's value must fully match to be considered valid.

questions.prompt: For a number or range input, which attributes together constrain the acceptable numeric range?
questions.explanation: min and max define the lower and upper bounds a numeric or range input's value must fall within to satisfy the range constraints.

questions.prompt: Which attribute controls the increment granularity that a number or range input's value must align to? (one word)
questions.explanation: step defines the legal value intervals (relative to min), so a value must be a multiple of step away from min to be considered valid.

questions.prompt: Which attribute caps the number of characters a text input or textarea will accept? (one word)
questions.explanation: maxlength sets the maximum number of characters the user can enter, enforced directly by the browser during typing.

questions.prompt: Which attribute sets a lower bound on the number of characters required for a text field to be valid?
questions.explanation: minlength specifies the fewest characters the value must contain to pass constraint validation; unlike maxlength, it does not stop the user from typing fewer, it only affects validity.

questions.prompt: Which button attribute lets a specific submit button bypass the form's normal validation for that one submission, without disabling validation for other buttons? (one word)
questions.explanation: formnovalidate, set on a submit button/input, disables constraint validation only for submissions triggered by that particular control, e.g. a 'Save draft' button.

questions.prompt: What is the constraint validation API method that returns whether a form control currently satisfies its constraints, without showing any UI?
questions.explanation: checkValidity() evaluates a control's (or form's) constraints and returns a boolean, firing an invalid event on failure but without necessarily surfacing UI, unlike reportValidity().

questions.prompt: Which CSS pseudo-classes let you style form fields based on whether they currently satisfy their validation constraints?
questions.explanation: :valid and :invalid match form elements based on whether their current value passes or fails constraint validation (required, pattern, min/max, etc.).

questions.prompt: Which attribute disables user interaction with a form control while still submitting no value for it at all?
questions.explanation: A disabled control cannot be focused, edited, or included in the form's submitted data at all.

questions.prompt: Which attribute keeps a field's existing value visible and prevents editing, while still submitting that value with the form?
questions.explanation: readonly leaves the control focusable and its value gets submitted, but the user cannot change it, unlike disabled which excludes the value from submission entirely.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on input restricts which file types a type="file" control will let the user select? (one word)
questions.explanation: accept takes a comma-separated list of file extensions or MIME types to filter the choices offered in the file picker.

questions.prompt: Which element defines a single row within a table? (one word)
questions.explanation: tr (table row) groups a set of td/th cells that make up one row of the table.

questions.prompt: Which element defines a standard data cell within a table row?
questions.explanation: td (table data) holds an ordinary data cell's content within a tr.

questions.prompt: Which element defines a header cell, which browsers render bold and centered by default and associate semantically with the data it describes? (one word)
questions.explanation: th marks a cell as a header for its row and/or column, giving assistive technology a way to associate data cells with the right header.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on th specifies whether it heades a row, a column, or a group of either?
questions.explanation: scope (with values like row, col, rowgroup, colgroup) tells assistive technology what the header cell applies to, which is especially useful for complex tables.

questions.prompt: Which attribute makes a table cell visually and semantically span across multiple columns? (one word)
questions.explanation: colspan takes an integer specifying how many columns a cell should span, merging that many column slots into one cell.

questions.prompt: Which attribute makes a table cell span across multiple rows?
questions.explanation: rowspan takes an integer specifying how many rows a cell should span vertically.

questions.prompt: Which element provides a title or description for an entire table, and must be its first child? (one word)
questions.explanation: caption, placed as the first child of table, provides a descriptive title for the whole table, both visually and for assistive technology.

questions.prompt: Which element groups the header row(s) of a table, separate from its body rows?
questions.explanation: thead groups the heading rows of a table, letting browsers (e.g. when printing across pages) and CSS treat them distinctly from the body.

questions.prompt: Which element groups the main data rows of a table, distinct from its header and footer? (one word)
questions.explanation: tbody groups one or more rows representing the primary content of a table.

questions.prompt: Which element groups summary or totals rows that appear logically at the end of a table, though it can be placed in the markup right after thead?
questions.explanation: tfoot groups a table's footer rows, such as column totals, and browsers render it after tbody's rows regardless of its position in the source.

questions.prompt: Which element wraps one or more col elements to apply shared styling/sizing to whole columns of a table at once?
questions.explanation: colgroup groups col elements, each of which can target styling (like width) at an entire column without repeating it per cell.

questions.prompt: Which three-letter element is the top-level container for an entire HTML table? (one word)
questions.explanation: table is the root element that contains a table's caption, column groups, head, body, and footer sections.

questions.prompt: Which attribute uniquely identifies a single element within a document, and must be unique across the whole page?
questions.explanation: id must be unique within the document and is commonly used as a target for CSS selectors, JavaScript lookups, and fragment links.

questions.prompt: Which attribute assigns one or more, space-separated, reusable names to an element for styling or scripting, and may repeat across many elements?
questions.explanation: class holds a space-separated list of class names, any of which can be shared by many elements, unlike the required-unique id attribute.

questions.prompt: Which family of attributes lets you attach custom, non-standard data to an element that scripts can read, without inventing new HTML attributes?
questions.explanation: Any attribute prefixed data- (e.g. data-user-id) is reserved for arbitrary custom data, readable in JavaScript via the dataset property.

questions.prompt: Which global attribute controls whether, and in what order, an element can be reached by pressing Tab? (one word)
questions.explanation: tabindex controls keyboard focusability and, when positive, an explicit tab order; tabindex="0" adds an element to the natural tab order without changing it.

questions.prompt: Which global boolean attribute hides an element from rendering and from most assistive technology, without needing any CSS? (one word)
questions.explanation: The hidden boolean attribute tells the browser not to render the element at all, roughly equivalent to display: none, without writing any CSS.

questions.prompt: Which global attribute provides extra advisory information about an element, most commonly shown as a tooltip on hover?
questions.explanation: The title global attribute supplies advisory text, which most browsers show as a hover tooltip, though it should not be relied on as the sole source of essential information.

questions.prompt: Which global attribute lets users directly edit the content of an element, turning it into a rich-text editing surface? (one word)
questions.explanation: contenteditable, set to true (or the empty string), makes an element's contents directly editable by the user in the rendered page.

questions.prompt: Which global boolean attribute allows an element to be picked up and moved using the native HTML drag-and-drop API?
questions.explanation: draggable="true" opts an element into being a valid source for the HTML Drag and Drop API.

questions.prompt: Which global attribute assigns a single keyboard shortcut key that activates or focuses an element? (one word)
questions.explanation: accesskey specifies a single character that, combined with a browser- and platform-specific modifier key, activates or focuses the element.

questions.prompt: Which global attribute controls whether a browser's built-in spelling and grammar checker examines an editable element's text?
questions.explanation: spellcheck, set to true or false, is a hint for whether the browser should run its spelling/grammar checker over that element's editable text.

questions.prompt: Which global attribute controls whether an element's text content should be translated when a page is machine-translated? (one word)
questions.explanation: translate, with values yes or no, hints to translation tools whether an element's content (e.g. a brand name) should be left untranslated.

questions.prompt: Which global attribute lets you apply inline CSS declarations directly to a single element, e.g. style="color: red;"? (one word)
questions.explanation: style holds inline CSS declarations that apply only to that one element, taking precedence over most external and internal stylesheet rules.

questions.prompt: What is the single most important thing that makes an img element accessible to screen reader users?
choices: A large width and height attribute
questions.explanation: Without a meaningful alt attribute, a screen reader has no textual content to announce for the image, so alt is the primary accessibility hook for img.

questions.prompt: Which attribute provides an accessible name for an element when there's no visible text to serve that purpose, such as an icon-only button? (include the aria- prefix)
questions.explanation: aria-label supplies a string used as the element's accessible name, overriding any visible text, which is useful when a control (like an icon button) has no text content of its own.

questions.prompt: Which attribute hides an element from assistive technology (like screen readers) while leaving it fully visible on screen? (include the aria- prefix)
questions.explanation: aria-hidden="true" removes an element from the accessibility tree without affecting its visual rendering, often used for purely decorative icons.

questions.prompt: Which attribute communicates to assistive technology that a collapsible section, like an accordion header, is currently open or closed? (include the aria- prefix)
questions.explanation: aria-expanded, set to true or false, reflects whether the control's associated collapsible content is currently expanded.

questions.prompt: Which attribute marks a region of the page so that screen readers announce updates within it automatically, even without focus moving there? (include the aria- prefix)
questions.explanation: aria-live, with values like polite or assertive, designates a live region whose content updates are automatically announced by assistive technology.

questions.prompt: What is the first rule of ARIA usage, often summarized as 'no ARIA is better than bad ARIA'?
choices: Always add role attributes to every element
Prefer a native HTML element or attribute with the semantics you need over adding an ARIA role/attribute to a generic element
ARIA should replace semantic HTML entirely
aria-* attributes only work inside forms
questions.explanation: Native elements (button, nav, input, etc.) come with built-in semantics, keyboard behavior, and accessible roles for free; ARIA should fill gaps, not replace native semantics that already exist.

questions.prompt: Which attribute overrides an element's default (or absent) accessible role, e.g. making a div behave like a button to assistive technology? (one word)
questions.explanation: The role attribute assigns an ARIA role, telling assistive technology what kind of widget or landmark the element represents.

questions.prompt: Which native element is equivalent to setting role="navigation" for free, without any ARIA attribute at all?
questions.explanation: The nav element has an implicit ARIA role of navigation, so wrapping navigation links in nav gives assistive technology the landmark for free.

questions.prompt: Which native element is equivalent to role="banner" when it is a direct child of body?
questions.explanation: A header element that isn't scoped inside another sectioning element maps to the banner landmark role, identifying the page's main header.

questions.prompt: Why is it problematic to add a click handler to a plain div to make it act like a button, without any further ARIA or attributes?
choices: It isn't, div elements are fully accessible by default
It has no accessible role, isn't keyboard-focusable, and doesn't respond to Enter/Space, unlike a real button
div elements cannot have click handlers attached
It only affects visual styling, not accessibility
questions.explanation: A bare div with a click handler has no button role for screen readers, isn't in the tab order, and won't activate on Enter or Space, so a real button (or role="button" plus manual tabindex and key handling) is needed for equivalent accessibility.

questions.prompt: Which attribute associates a form control with one or more elements elsewhere on the page that describe it, such as a hint or error message? (include the aria- prefix)
questions.explanation: aria-describedby references the id(s) of elements providing extra descriptive text (like hint or validation text), read after the accessible name.

questions.prompt: Which attribute lets you provide an accessible name for an element by referencing the id of another visible element, instead of duplicating the text? (include the aria- prefix)
questions.explanation: aria-labelledby points to the id(s) of element(s) whose text content should be used as this element's accessible name.

questions.prompt: Why is placeholder text alone not a sufficient substitute for a proper label on an input?
choices: placeholder text is not read by any browser
placeholder disappears once the user starts typing and is not reliably announced as a persistent accessible name by all assistive tech
placeholder can only be used on textarea
questions.explanation: Placeholder text vanishes once input begins, offers low contrast by default, and support for exposing it as an accessible name is inconsistent, so a real label element (or aria-label) should still be provided.

questions.prompt: Which ARIA attribute would you add to a custom slider widget built from div elements to expose its current numeric value to assistive technology?
questions.explanation: A custom slider needs role="slider" plus aria-valuenow (and typically aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax) so assistive technology can report its current position, since native input type="range" provides all of this for free.

questions.prompt: Which native form element gives you a labeled group of controls, plus an accessible group name from its legend, without any ARIA?
questions.explanation: fieldset paired with legend is the native way to group related controls (like a set of radio buttons) and give that group an accessible name, all without ARIA.

questions.prompt: Which attribute indicates to assistive technology that a region of the page is currently being updated and its content should be treated as not yet ready? (include the aria- prefix)
questions.explanation: aria-busy="true" signals that an element is actively being modified and screen readers should hold off announcing changes until it's set back to false.

questions.prompt: Which meta attribute combination sets the responsive viewport behavior commonly used on mobile-friendly pages?
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag with width=device-width and initial-scale=1 tells mobile browsers to match the layout viewport to the device's width instead of zooming out to a desktop-width layout.

questions.prompt: Which meta name is conventionally used to provide a short summary of the page for search engine results snippets? (one word)
questions.explanation: meta name="description" content="..." supplies a short page summary that search engines often display as the results snippet.

questions.prompt: Which link relation is used to point the browser to a page's favicon? (one word, the rel value only)
questions.explanation: link rel="icon" href="..." tells the browser which image to use as the page/tab icon; the older rel="shortcut icon" form still works but is unnecessary today.

questions.prompt: Which link relation attaches an external CSS file to a document? (one word, the rel value only)
questions.explanation: link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css" loads and applies an external stylesheet to the document.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on script prevents it from blocking HTML parsing, while still guaranteeing it runs in source order before DOMContentLoaded? (one word)
questions.explanation: defer lets the browser keep parsing HTML while the script downloads, then runs it in document order right before DOMContentLoaded fires.

questions.prompt: How does script async differ from script defer?
choices: async runs the script as soon as it's downloaded, potentially out of order relative to other scripts and before parsing finishes; defer waits and preserves order
async only works on external scripts, defer only on inline scripts
defer blocks parsing, async never does
questions.explanation: async scripts execute as soon as they finish downloading, interrupting parsing wherever it happens to be and with no guaranteed order relative to other async scripts; defer preserves execution order and always waits until after parsing.

questions.prompt: Which meta http-equiv value can be used to redirect the browser to another URL after a delay, entirely without JavaScript?
questions.explanation: meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5;url=https://example.com" tells the browser to navigate to the given URL after the specified number of seconds.

questions.prompt: Which element, placed in head, provides fallback content shown only when JavaScript is disabled or unsupported?
questions.explanation: noscript's content is only rendered by browsers that have scripting disabled or don't support it, offering a fallback message or content.

questions.prompt: Which link relation hints the browser to establish an early connection to a third-party origin before a resource from it is actually requested?
questions.explanation: rel="preconnect" tells the browser to start the connection handshake (DNS, TCP, TLS) to a given origin early, reducing latency once a resource from it is actually needed.

questions.prompt: Which link relation tells the browser to fetch and cache a specific resource early because it will definitely be needed soon, without executing or applying it yet? (one word, the rel value only)
questions.explanation: rel="preload" requests the browser fetch a specific resource (with an as attribute describing its type) at high priority well before it's referenced elsewhere, without yet running or applying it.

questions.prompt: Which element embeds another full HTML document inside the current page, as a nested browsing context? (one word)
questions.explanation: iframe embeds another HTML document within the current page, functioning as its own nested browsing context.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on iframe restricts what the embedded document is allowed to do, such as running scripts or submitting forms? (one word)
questions.explanation: sandbox applies a set of extra restrictions to an iframe's content; an empty sandbox attribute applies all restrictions, and specific tokens (like allow-scripts) can re-enable individual capabilities.

questions.prompt: Which element is the generic mechanism for embedding external content handled by a plugin or the browser itself, such as a PDF?
choices: Both embed and object can serve this purpose
questions.explanation: Both embed and object can embed external resources like PDFs or other media types handled outside normal HTML rendering; object additionally supports fallback content between its tags.

questions.prompt: Which element holds markup that is parsed by the browser but not rendered or executed until JavaScript explicitly clones and inserts its contents? (one word)
questions.explanation: template's content is inert HTML, parsed and validated but never rendered on its own; scripts typically clone template.content and insert it into the DOM when needed.

questions.prompt: Which script attribute marks the block as JSON or a non-executable data payload rather than JavaScript to run?
questions.explanation: Setting script's type to a non-executable value like application/json prevents the browser from trying to run it as JavaScript, letting it serve purely as embedded structured data that scripts can read.

questions.prompt: Why might a developer choose object over img for an SVG image specifically?
choices: object cannot display images at all
object lets the embedded SVG's own scripts and internal links run and be interacted with, unlike img which treats SVG as a static image
object is faster to load in every case
There is no difference between img and object for SVG
questions.explanation: Loading an SVG via object (or iframe) preserves its interactivity, letting internal scripts, links, and CSS animations inside the SVG function, whereas img always renders SVG as a flattened, non-interactive image.

questions.prompt: Which attribute of script points to an external JavaScript file rather than inlining code between the tags? (one word)
questions.explanation: src on script specifies the URL of an external script file to fetch and execute, instead of using the element's inline text content.

questions.prompt: What happens if a script element has both a src attribute and inline text content between its tags?
choices: Both run, inline code first then the external file
Both run, the external file first then inline code
The inline content is ignored entirely; only the external file referenced by src executes
questions.explanation: When src is present, the browser fetches and executes that external resource and ignores any inline text content the script element might also contain.

questions.prompt: Which element creates a native, disclosure widget that can be toggled open and closed without any JavaScript? (one word)
questions.explanation: details creates a collapsible disclosure widget; clicking its summary child toggles the open attribute, showing or hiding the rest of its content.

questions.prompt: Inside a details element, which element provides the always-visible label the user clicks to expand or collapse it? (one word)
questions.explanation: summary is the visible, clickable label for a details element; if omitted, browsers supply a default label like 'Details'.

questions.prompt: Which element natively implements a modal or non-modal popup dialog, including its own top-layer rendering and backdrop when shown modally?
questions.explanation: dialog provides a native dialog box; calling its showModal() method renders it modally with a ::backdrop, focus trapping, and top-layer stacking handled by the browser.

questions.prompt: Which element visually represents the completion progress of a task, like a file upload, toward a set value? (one word)
questions.explanation: progress displays how far a task has advanced toward completion, taking a value and an optional max.

questions.prompt: Which element represents a scalar measurement within a known range, such as disk usage, rather than task completion?
questions.explanation: meter represents a fixed-range gauge-style measurement (like disk space used) rather than a task's completion progress, which is what progress is for.

questions.prompt: Which element displays the live result of a calculation, often updated by script in response to user input, such as a form's computed total? (one word)
questions.explanation: output is used to display the result of a calculation or user action, and can be associated with the controls that produced its value via a for attribute.

questions.prompt: Which element defines a set of predefined autocomplete suggestions for a paired text input, without forcing the user to pick only from that list?
questions.explanation: datalist holds a set of option elements offering suggestions; when referenced by an input's list attribute, the user gets autocomplete-style suggestions but can still type any other value.

questions.prompt: Which attribute on input associates it with a datalist element to supply autocomplete suggestions?
questions.explanation: The list attribute on input takes the id of a datalist element, wiring up its option values as suggestions for that field.

questions.prompt: Which named HTML character entity is used to display a literal ampersand character? (include the leading & and trailing ;)
questions.explanation: & renders as a literal & character; a raw & in text can otherwise start an entity reference and cause ambiguous parsing.

questions.prompt: Which named HTML character entity displays a literal less-than sign without the browser mistaking it for the start of a tag? (include the leading & and trailing ;)
questions.explanation: < renders as a literal < character, since a bare < in text content would otherwise be interpreted as beginning a tag.

questions.prompt: Besides named entities like &, what is the other general syntax for writing a character reference in HTML, useful for characters without a common name?
choices: A numeric character reference, like é or é
questions.explanation: HTML also supports numeric character references, either decimal (é) or hexadecimal (é), which specify a character by its Unicode code point.

questions.prompt: Which named entity produces a non-breaking space, which prevents a line break at that point and is not collapsed like a normal space? (include the leading & and trailing ;)
questions.explanation: inserts a non-breaking space: it displays as a normal space but browsers won't wrap a line at it, and consecutive ones are not collapsed the way regular whitespace is.

questions.prompt: Why can't you always write a literal < character directly in HTML text content?
choices: A bare < can be interpreted as the start of a tag, so it should be escaped as < in text
< is only invalid inside attributes, never in text
There is no restriction at all
questions.explanation: Because < signals the start of a markup tag to the HTML parser, a literal < intended as text should be written as the < entity to avoid being parsed as markup.

questions.prompt: Why must attribute values that contain a double quote character be handled carefully, e.g. title="She said "hi""?
choices: Double quotes are never allowed in attribute values
An unescaped literal double quote inside a double-quoted attribute value would prematurely terminate that attribute
" is required even in single-quoted attributes
This only matters for XML, not HTML
questions.explanation: If an attribute's value is delimited with double quotes, a literal unescaped double quote inside it would end the attribute early, so it must be written as " (or the whole attribute switched to single quotes).

questions.prompt: Which presentational element, once used to set typeface/size/color directly in markup, has been removed from the HTML5 specification in favor of CSS? (one word)
questions.explanation: font, which set typeface, size, and color directly in markup, was removed from the HTML5 spec; the same effects should be achieved with CSS instead.

questions.prompt: Which obsolete element used to center-align its contents, and should now be replaced with CSS text-align or margin auto? (one word)
questions.explanation: center was a purely presentational element for centering content, removed in favor of CSS-based layout and text alignment.

questions.prompt: Which obsolete, non-standard element made its text scroll or slide across the page automatically? (one word)
questions.explanation: marquee was a non-standard, now-obsolete element for automatically scrolling text; it is broadly discouraged for both usability and accessibility reasons.

questions.prompt: Which pair of elements, used to split a browser window into independently scrollable panes, are obsolete in modern HTML5 in favor of techniques like CSS layout or iframe?
questions.explanation: frame and frameset, which split the window into a rigid grid of separately navigable panes, are obsolete; iframe remains available for embedding a single external document within the flow of a page.

questions.prompt: The align attribute, once usable directly on elements like img or table to control alignment, is now considered what?
choices: Still the recommended, primary way to align elements
Obsolete; alignment should be handled with CSS instead
questions.explanation: Presentational attributes like align were removed or deprecated across HTML5 in favor of doing all visual alignment and layout through CSS.

questions.prompt: Why do modern style guides discourage inline event-handler attributes like onclick="doSomething()" directly in HTML markup, even though they still technically work?
choices: Browsers no longer execute them at all
They mix behavior into markup, complicate Content-Security-Policy that disallows inline scripts, and make code harder to maintain than attaching listeners in JavaScript
They are invalid HTML and fail validation entirely
They only function inside iframe elements
questions.explanation: While still valid HTML and functional, inline event-handler attributes tightly couple behavior to markup, are typically blocked by a strict Content-Security-Policy, and are generally considered worse practice than using addEventListener in a separate script.

questions.prompt: What best describes the current governance model of the HTML specification?
choices: A single, versioned standard frozen at HTML5 by W3C
A continuously updated 'living standard' maintained by WHATWG
A closed specification controlled by one browser vendor
There is no formal specification; it's set entirely by convention
questions.explanation: Since 2019, the WHATWG's HTML Living Standard is the single canonical specification, continuously revised, rather than being versioned into discrete numbered releases like the old HTML5/4.01 model.

questions.prompt: What distinguished XHTML from regular HTML, historically?
choices: XHTML required documents to be well-formed, strict XML, e.g. all tags closed and lowercase
XHTML allowed more relaxed, forgiving syntax than HTML
XHTML removed the need for a doctype
XHTML and HTML are exact synonyms with no differences
questions.explanation: XHTML reformulated HTML as an application of XML, requiring strict well-formedness, such as properly closed and nested tags and lowercase element names, which a browser's HTML parser would otherwise tolerate being sloppy about.

questions.prompt: Which two-letter void element inserts a line break and, being a void element, never has a closing tag? (one word)
questions.explanation: br is a void element: it never has content or a closing tag, unlike container elements such as div, span, or p.

questions.prompt: Is writing a void element with a trailing slash, like a self-closing br in XML style, required in plain HTML (not XHTML)?
choices: Yes, omitting the slash is a parse error
No, HTML's parser treats void elements as self-closing regardless of a trailing slash; the slash is optional and purely stylistic
It changes the element into a different tag entirely
questions.explanation: In HTML's parsing algorithm, void elements like br, img, and hr are inherently self-closing; an optional trailing slash is permitted for familiarity with XML/XHTML but has no effect on parsing.
